If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the curves $y={x}^{3}$ and $y=\sqrt{x},$ as shown above, then ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA=$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's represent $D$ as a type I region. To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14150437/assets/8f18afd79cafdcd0696b3bc25c05fec4109e54cccb084eef49544a4d6599526c.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{3}\le y\le \sqrt{x}\}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{3}}^{\sqrt{x}}f(x,y)\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{{x}^{3}}^{\sqrt{x}}f(x,y)\,dy]dx\end{aligned}
$$
